metadata.title: West Bengal Soils - Part 4: Bengal Basin (Including Coastal and Tidal Zones)
metadata.region_covered: North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, Howrah, Nadia (southern parts), Sundarban
metadata.source: National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (ICAR), Nagpur
metadata.special_note: Includes unique coastal, tidal, and saline soils of Sundarban region

properties.soil_name: Dark grey to black clayey soils, Basin depression soils
properties.parent_material: Fine-textured old alluvium in depressional basins
properties.rooting_depth: Shallow to moderate (40-80cm, severely restricted by poor drainage)
properties.land_use: Paddy (single crop), Wetland vegetation, Fish farming
properties.land_capability: Class III-IV (Suitable only for wetland rice)
properties.limitations: Poor to very poor drainage, Heavy texture, Very slow permeability, Prolonged waterlogging (6-9 months), Near-impossible tillage
properties.management_practices: Suitable for wetland rice only, Fish farming in deeper areas, Integrated rice-fish farming
properties.productivity_rating: Medium for deepwater rice, High for integrated rice-fish systems
properties.description: Very deep, poorly drained, fine (clayey) soils on nearly level to depressional basins; slightly acidic to slightly alkaline reaction. These permanently waterlogged soils are suitable only for deepwater rice or fish farming.

properties.soil_name: Grey to dark grey clayey soils
properties.land_use: Paddy (single to double crop), Jute, Vegetables (limited)
properties.land_capability: Class II-III (Good for rice, limited for others)
properties.irrigation_suitability: Not needed for kharif, drainage needed for rabi
properties.limitations: Poor drainage, Heavy texture, Slow permeability, Seasonal waterlogging (4-7 months), Slight to moderate alkalinity in some areas
properties.management_practices: Drainage improvement, Green manuring, Timely transplanting, Zinc and sulphur application, Salt-tolerant varieties in affected areas
properties.productivity_rating: High for rice, Low to medium for dry crops
properties.description: Very deep, poorly drained, fine (clayey) soils on nearly level to depressional basins; slightly acidic to moderately alkaline reaction. These soils are extensively used for rice cultivation but have severe limitations for dry season crops without proper drainage.

properties.soil_name: Dark grey to black heavy clayey soils, Marsh soils
properties.slope_class: Nearly level to depressional marshy areas
properties.land_use: Deepwater paddy, Wetland, Fish farming, Limited agriculture
properties.limitations: Permanent waterlogging, Very heavy texture, Extremely slow permeability, High organic matter decomposition under anaerobic conditions, Methane emission
properties.management_practices: Deepwater rice varieties, Integrated rice-fish farming, Wetland conservation, No scope for dry season crops
properties.productivity_rating: Low for crops, High for integrated rice-fish systems
properties.description: Very deep, poorly to very poorly drained, fine (heavy clayey) soils on nearly level to depressional marshy areas; slightly acidic to moderately alkaline reaction. These permanently waterlogged soils are unsuitable for conventional agriculture and are best utilized for wetland conservation or integrated rice-fish farming.

properties.soil_name: Grey to brownish grey clayey soils
properties.slope: Nearly level to very gently sloping (0-1%)
properties.slope_class: Nearly level to very gently sloping coastal plains
properties.land_capability: Class II-III (Good for rice and vegetables)
properties.irrigation_suitability: Moderate - drainage needed in wet season
properties.limitations: Poor drainage, Heavy texture, Slight salinity risk in dry season, Cyclone and storm surge vulnerability
properties.management_practices: Drainage improvement, Salt-tolerant varieties near coast, Betel leaf cultivation in suitable areas, Protective embankments
properties.description: Very deep, poorly drained, fine (clayey) soils on nearly level to very gently sloping coastal plains; slightly acidic to neutral reaction. These productive soils support intensive rice and vegetable cultivation with proper water management.

properties.soil_name: Grey to dark grey clayey soils, Tidal plain soils
properties.land_capability: Class III-IV (Moderate for rice, limited for others)
properties.limitations: Tidal inundation, Poor drainage, Salinity (seasonal to permanent), Acid sulphate risk, Cyclone vulnerability, Limited freshwater availability
properties.management_practices: Embankment protection, Tidal water management, Salt-tolerant rice varieties, Integrated rice-fish farming, Mangrove afforestation
properties.productivity_rating: Medium for rice, High for aquaculture
properties.description: Very deep, poorly drained, fine (clayey) soils on nearly level tidal fluvio-marine plains; slightly acidic to moderately alkaline reaction. These soils are influenced by tidal action and require special management for sustainable agriculture and aquaculture.

properties.region: Bengal Basin - Active Tidal Coastal Zone (Sundarban)
properties.soil_name: Dark grey to black saline clayey soils, Coastal saline soils
properties.parent_material: Marine sediments with high salt content
properties.slope_class: Nearly level tidal affected coastal plains
properties.rooting_depth: Very shallow to shallow (20-60cm, severely restricted by salinity)
properties.land_use: Mangrove forest, Saline aquaculture, Limited agriculture with salt-tolerant varieties
properties.limitations: Strong salinity, Tidal inundation twice daily, Very poor drainage, Acid sulphate potential, Severe cyclone risk, Coastal erosion, Limited freshwater
properties.management_practices: Mangrove conservation (critical), Saline aquaculture (prawns, crabs), Embankment maintenance, Salt-tolerant forestry, No conventional agriculture

marginally_suitable: Salt-tolerant paddy (only behind embankments with freshwater)

properties.productivity_rating: Very high for mangrove ecosystem services, High for aquaculture, Not suitable for agriculture
properties.conservation_importance: Critical for coastal protection, biodiversity hotspot, UNESCO World Heritage Site (Sundarban)
properties.description: Very deep, poorly to very poorly drained, fine (heavy clayey) soils on tidal affected nearly level coastal plains; strongly saline soils. These soils form part of the Sundarban ecosystem and are unsuitable for agriculture but critical for mangrove conservation and coastal protection.
